key_insight: SMAW produced a sound weld on low-carbon steel pipeline with acceptable strength, toughness, and bend performance despite some hardness variation across weld zones.
engineering_relevance: The results support SMAW as a practical joining method for pipeline fabrication and repair when weld integrity is verified through mechanical testing.
method: Destructive testing of the welded joint: hardness, tensile, Charpy impact, and bend tests
Micro/macro hardness assessment across weld metal (WM), heat-affected zone (HAZ), and base metal (BM)
Macro examination of weld geometry and penetration depth
evidence_signal: The weld showed UTS around 566–569 N/mm², Charpy energy of 132.9 J in WM versus 237.1 J in HAZ and 247.4 J in BM, and adequate penetration of about 5.8 mm with no cracking in bend tests.
watch_item: Results are based on a limited set of specimens and one pipeline material, so weld performance may vary with electrode type, operator skill, and field conditions.
paper_title: Investigation of Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)Weld Integrity on a Low- Carbon Steel Pipeline using Destructive Mechanical Testing Technique
